_comment: sim/cmrr-psrr PSRR as a `klt sim` request (issue #99): the supply-gain half of the PSRR row. REQUEST COVERAGE ONLY -- no envelope has been committed from this request.
Circuit: tb_psrr.body.spice -- the same test circuit as ../testbench/tb_psrr.spice.tmpl (Vdd carries ac 1; the signal input is AC-quiet).
Grid: cornerMOSlv.lib mos_tt/ss/ff/sf/fs [DR-1] x {-40, 27, 125} C x VDD {1.08, 1.20, 1.32} V = 45 corners.
vinp sweeps WITH vdd by index (klt's supply_v semantics), so Vcm = VDD/2 at every corner, as in the harness.
Each process corner is a bundle carrying the template's fixed cornerCAP.lib cap_typ section (the Miller cap is a cap_cmim MIM device).
Analysis: ac dec 20 10m 1g = the template's sweep. The DC shelf is read at 10 mHz (below the ~1.5 Hz supply zero), as in the harness.
Ratified row: PSRR+ (DC shelf) >= 1.87 dB worst-case [DR-2] (spec/target-spec.md section 2), PSRR = Av0 - Avs0 in dB at the same point.

ENCODING OF THE BOUND: PSRR is a ratio of two different AC excitations (Av0: Vinp ac 1; Avs: Vdd ac 1). One AC solve cannot carry both, and `limits` are per measurement of THIS request, so the bound is NOT a `limits` entry here.

This request reports avs0_db (and avs_1khz_db) only. compare.py joins the same-point Av0 from sim/open-loop-ac/records/20260910-221601-22feaba.csv (harness evidence, not a `klt sim` Av0 envelope) and applies PSRR >= 1.87 dB offline.
That offline verdict is NOT a klt verdict. Do not describe this request as a single-solve PSRR ratio.

A bound expressed per corner as avs0_db <= Av0(corner) - 1.87 would need a per-corner limit, which the request schema does not have; a single corner-independent substitute would change the bound's meaning, so none is used.

Checked limit that makes coverage.nothing_checked false: the harness's own plateau guard (|Avs(10 mHz) - Avs(0.1 Hz)| <= 0.05 dB, flat-shelf check). The harness record documents one point (mos_ss_-40C_1.08V) at 0.066 dB; a miss there is a result, not hidden (compare.py cross-checks it against the harness flag).
Solver tolerance: ngspice default, no .options reltol/abstol/vntol (DR-0005).
ngspice_init raises the printed digits only (measureprec for .meas, numdgt for expr); it changes no solver setting.
keep_artifacts is false so the committed envelope carries no host-absolute artifact paths.
